This video gives a good answers to the question I got from my managers how many FTE's we saved using AI. Think the equation is faulty, but could not explain it in any good way for my manager. No FTA's are saved. And we can't compare the how much more we do with or without AI, because we do things better than before. We delivery things that we did not have the knowledge for before, and we would not pay people to do it before AI. It creates value for the customers but only now it made sense to deliver this marginal value because it was to expensive or to hard to to do before.

The big argument this video overlooks is that AI and other technologies increase productivity and can lead to the creation of more jobs… This leads to an increase of scale and thus an increase in profits. The Washington Post might employ more people than it did 60 years ago, but are its employees more financially stable? This is because the efficiency created by new technology results in a time savings that does not get passed along to workers. If I’m 20% more efficient at my job because I use AI, I don’t get to work 32 hours a week. I’m expected to fill those 8 hours with additional work. Usually, the best result I can hope for in that scenario is that my efficiency is recognized in the form of an annual raise that is provided after months of working at this increased efficiency and likely won’t be a 20% increase. This is why every day people don’t see the “competitive advantages” of AI the way that employers and shareholders do. Time saved performing tedious tasks is simply filled with other tedious tasks, not leisure or fulfilling tasks. Related side note: My uncle is an elevator operator.
